transcript:
Doctor: What brought you in this afternoon?
Patient: A sore throat. It has been bothering me for three days.
Doctor: How would you describe how bad it feels?
Patient: Moderate, especially when I swallow.
Doctor: Have you tried anything for it?
Patient: I've been using throat lozenges.
Doctor: Any allergies to medicines?
Patient: I have no medication allergies.

Doctor: Tell me what is bothering you.
Patient: My left ankle is sore.
Doctor: When did that start?
Patient: Yesterday afternoon, after I got home.
Doctor: How bad is the soreness, and have you tried treating it?
Patient: It's mild. I haven't taken or applied anything for it.
Doctor: What should I put in the medicine allergy box?
Patient: Penicillin gives me hives.

Doctor: How have you been feeling?
Patient: Nausea and bloating are the reason I came.
Doctor: Give me a sense of the timing and intensity.
Patient: Two days so far. I'd call it five out of ten.
Doctor: What have you done to try to settle it?
Patient: I tried peppermint tea.
Doctor: Before we finish the history, are you allergic to any medicines?
Patient: No, I'm not allergic to any medicines.

Doctor: What would you like us to look at today?
Patient: This itchy rash on my forearm has been here a week.
Doctor: Does the itching feel mild, moderate, or severe?
Patient: Mild is the right word.
Doctor: Anything you've put on it or taken for it?
Patient: Nothing at all for this rash.
Doctor: Tell me about medication allergies.
Patient: There aren't any; I don't have medication allergies.

Doctor: What has been happening?
Patient: I've got a headache across my forehead.
Doctor: How long has that been going on?
Patient: Two days, or perhaps three. I can't pin down which day it started.
Doctor: And how bad is it?
Patient: I honestly can't decide whether to call it mild or moderate.
Doctor: Have you tried anything for the headache?
Patient: Acetaminophen, one time yesterday.
Doctor: Do you have medication allergies?
Patient: I can't remember whether I have any.

Doctor: What is the main problem?
Patient: I can't tell if it's an earache or pain in my jaw.
Doctor: When did you first notice that discomfort?
Patient: Four days ago.
Doctor: How strong does it feel?
Patient: Mild, but annoying.
Doctor: Anything taken for it?
Patient: I may have taken a tablet for it yesterday, but I can't remember whether I actually did.
Doctor: Any allergies you want recorded?
Patient: I'm allergic to latex.

Doctor: What's your concern today?
Patient: A dry cough.
Doctor: How long have you had it, and how bad is it?
Patient: I don't know when it started. It's three out of ten for how much it bothers me.
Doctor: Have you used any cough medicine?
Patient: I remember getting the syrup out, but I'm not sure whether I swallowed any.
Doctor: Do you know of any medicine allergies?
Patient: I don't know my medicine allergy history.

Doctor: What would you like to discuss?
Patient: Stomach cramps, starting the evening before last.
Doctor: How would you rate them?
Patient: Somewhere between mild and moderate; I can't choose one.
Doctor: What have you tried for the cramps?
Patient: I took ibuprofen and an antacid for them yesterday.
Doctor: Any medicine or material allergies?
Patient: I'm allergic to penicillin and latex.

Doctor: What is the new concern?
Patient: My neck has felt stiff since I woke up this morning.
Doctor: How uncomfortable is it?
Patient: Only mildly uncomfortable.
Doctor: Have you taken anything for your neck?
Patient: No, I haven't used anything for the neck stiffness. I do take my thyroid tablet every morning.
Doctor: So the thyroid tablet is part of your usual routine?
Patient: Yes, it isn't something I took for my neck.
Doctor: Do you have allergies to medicines?
Patient: I have no allergies to medicines.

Doctor: Tell me about the problem you're here for.
Patient: My right elbow aches. It started four days ago and feels moderate.
Doctor: What have you taken for that ache?
Patient: Naproxen yesterday.
Doctor: I see a mention of nausea with codeine in the old history. What does that refer to?
Patient: Codeine upset my stomach years ago. I'm describing a side effect, not an allergy.
Doctor: Do you have any medication allergies?
Patient: I don't have any medication allergies.

Doctor: What has changed recently?
Patient: My shoulder started aching two days ago.
Doctor: How bad is the current ache?
Patient: About four out of ten.
Doctor: Have you tried medicine for it?
Patient: I took ibuprofen for a shoulder injury last winter. For this new ache, I haven't tried any treatment.
Doctor: What about medicine allergies?
Patient: I had a rash as a child, but I don't know whether an antibiotic or a new soap caused it.

Doctor: What's been troubling you?
Patient: A toothache for two days.
Doctor: How bad would you say it is?
Patient: Seven out of ten.
Doctor: Any tablets or other treatment for this toothache?
Patient: I took one tablet from a packet the dentist gave me before, but I cannot remember its name.
Doctor: Are you allergic to any medicines?
Patient: I am not allergic to any medicines.

Doctor: What brought you here?
Patient: A headache. This headache began two days ago.
Doctor: Where do you feel it, and how bad is it?
Patient: Mostly at the back of my head. It is mild.
Doctor: Have you taken or used anything for it?
Patient: I haven't used any treatment for it.
Doctor: Any allergies to medicine?
Patient: No medication allergies.
Doctor: Before I finish this part, tell me again when this same headache began.
Patient: This headache began five days ago.

Doctor: What's bothering you?
Patient: An itchy patch on my left calf, for one week.
Doctor: How much does it bother you?
Patient: It's mild.
Doctor: Have you treated this itch at all during this week?
Patient: I haven't taken or applied anything for this itch at any point this week.
Doctor: Do you have medication allergies?
Patient: I have no drug allergies.
Doctor: Walk me through your evening routine while you've had this patch.
Patient: I used hydrocortisone on this itch every night this week.

Doctor: Which problem are we looking at today?
Patient: My right wrist hurts right now; my left wrist doesn't hurt.
Doctor: When did the wrist pain begin?
Patient: Last night. Sorry, that was the other thing I was thinking of. The wrist pain began this morning.
Doctor: How bad is it, and have you tried anything?
Patient: It's moderate. I haven't tried anything for it.
Doctor: Tell me which wrist is painful right now as I write this down.
Patient: My left wrist hurts right now; my right wrist doesn't hurt.

Doctor: What is the reason for your visit?
Patient: A runny nose. I've had it for six days.
Doctor: How bad has it been today?
Patient: It has been mild all day today.
Doctor: What have you used for it?
Patient: A saline spray.
Doctor: Any medicine allergies?
Patient: I said aspirin on the intake form, but that was a mistake. Penicillin is the medicine I'm allergic to.
Doctor: Describe today's severity once more for the note.
Patient: It has been severe all day today.

Doctor: Tell me what brought you in.
Patient: My knee aches, and it has been doing that for three days.
Other: I'm here to drive her home. My own migraines are severe, so I know what it's like to wait for an appointment.
Doctor: Let's come back to your knee. How bad is the ache?
Patient: Mild.
Doctor: Have you treated it at home?
Patient: I haven't tried any treatment for it.
Doctor: Any medicine allergies for you?
Patient: I don't have any.

Doctor: What is your main concern?
Patient: Numbness in my right hand.
Doctor: How long has the numbness been there?
Other: Excuse me, the parking meter is about to run out.
Patient: The keys are in the side pocket of my bag.
Doctor: Is the ibuprofen bottle on the desk yours?
Patient: No, that's my husband's bottle for his back.
Doctor: I also see a family history note about aspirin.
Patient: My sister is allergic to aspirin. She's the one that note is about.

Doctor: The booking message says a severe sore throat for a week. Can you describe the problem in your own words?
Patient: A scratchy throat is what I'm here about.
Doctor: Anything else you'd like me to know before we go through it?
Patient: The dizziness from last spring has gone away. I had that for a month, but it's unrelated to why I booked today.
Doctor: Let's check the allergy history while the booking message loads.
Patient: I can't tell you whether I'm allergic to penicillin; my family gave me different accounts.
Doctor: Is this still your current address on the screen?
Patient: Yes, apartment six, not apartment nine.

Doctor: How can I help with today's concern?
Patient: I've felt dizzy since this morning.
Doctor: How severe is that feeling?
Patient: I find it hard to judge. I can't put it into mild, moderate, or severe.
Other: For my own appointments I always say severe. And I have a latex allergy, if you're asking the whole family.
Doctor: I'm taking this patient's history first.
Patient: My brother does like to talk. We came together on the bus.
Doctor: We'll continue the history after I check the room number.

Doctor: What problem would you like to start with?
Patient: A persistent cough.
Doctor: How long has it been going on, how bad is it, and what have you tried?
Patient: I haven't tried any treatment for the cough.
Doctor: All right, let me get those other questions down as well.
Patient: Could you move the chair a little closer? I have trouble hearing from here.
Doctor: Is that better?
Patient: Yes, I can hear you now.

Doctor: Tell me what's wrong, when it began, anything you've taken, and any medicine allergies.
Patient: My left ear is ringing. I'm allergic to sulfa antibiotics.
Doctor: How much is the ringing bothering you?
Patient: Could we start by checking whether I can hear properly?
Doctor: I'll write down that request. Are you comfortable in that chair?
Patient: Yes, thank you.
Doctor: I need to bring up the rest of the intake page.
Patient: Take your time.

Doctor: What has been happening, and when did it start?
Patient: Spasms in my lower back. Maybe last Tuesday, maybe the Thursday before that; I can't remember.
Doctor: How bad are they, and what have you tried for them?
Patient: I haven't taken or used anything for them.
Doctor: What about allergies to medicines?
Patient: Sorry, that's my phone ringing. It's the person who's picking me up.
Doctor: Do you need a moment to answer?
Patient: Yes, just a moment, please.

Doctor: What would you like to talk about today?
Patient: Pressure behind both eyes.
Doctor: How long has it lasted, how bad is it, have you taken anything for it, and do you have medication allergies?
Patient: Four days, and I have no medication allergies.
Doctor: You mentioned travel when you checked in.
Patient: Yes, I returned on Sunday. Actually, I checked the ticket: I returned on Saturday.
Doctor: Was it a long trip home?
Patient: Most of the afternoon, with a train change in the middle.
